senses.definition: A plant with simple stems, like bamboo or sugar cane, or the stem thereof:

subsenses.definition: (uncountable) The slender, flexible main stem of a plant such as bamboo, including many species in the grass family Gramineae.
(uncountable) The plant itself, including many species in the grass family Gramineae; a reed.

quotes.text: Still, a dozen men with rifles, and cartridges to match, stayed behind when they filed through a white aldea lying silent amid the cane, and the Sin Verguenza swung into slightly quicker stride.

subsenses.definition: (US, Southern) Maize or, rarely, sorghum, when such plants are processed to make molasses (treacle) or sugar.

senses.definition: The stem of such a plant adapted for use as a tool:

subsenses.definition: (countable) A short rod or stick, traditionally of wood or bamboo, used for corporal punishment.

quotes.text: He stalked behind her simple narrative, a kill-joy parent, hasty, intolerant, keeping a special cane to enforce the authority of his sadistic God[.]

subsenses.definition: (with "the") Corporal punishment by beating with a cane.
examples: The teacher gave his student the cane for throwing paper.

subsenses.definition: A lance or dart made of cane.

quotes.text: Judgelike thou sitt'st, to praise or to arraign / The flying skirmish of the darted cane.

senses.definition: A rod-shaped tool or device, resembling the stem of the plant:

subsenses.definition: (countable) A strong short staff used for support or decoration during walking; a walking stick.
examples: After breaking his leg, he needed a cane to walk.

quotes.text: The cane was undoubtedly of foreign make, for it had a solid silver ferrule at one end, which was not English hall–marked.

(countable) A long rod often collapsible and commonly white (for visibility to other persons), used by vision impaired persons for guidance in determining their course and for probing for obstacles in their path.

senses.definition: (uncountable) Split rattan, as used in wickerwork and basketry.

senses.definition: (UK, New Zealand, slang) To destroy; to comprehensively defeat.
(UK, New Zealand, slang) To do something well, in a competent fashion.
